subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the macOS Dashboard browser auth surface be shared-token/password only, or may it inject native device/operator tokens for parity with native clients?
rationale: The two open same-surface PRs encode opposite credential-boundary policies, and automation cannot choose whether native device tokens are allowed to cross into embedded browser Control UI auth.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Require this PR or its replacement to update all Dashboard injection paths, including endpoint reload, and prove shared-token/password behavior on macOS before merge.

options.title: Keep native-token parity
options.body: Close or pause this PR and continue with the sibling parity work so browser Dashboard auth can use the same resolved native/operator token path as native clients.

options.title: Accept the upgrade break explicitly
options.body: Maintainers can choose shared-token-only even if existing no-shared-token users lose automatic browser auth, but the PR should state that product decision and prove the new recovery path.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Require this PR or its replacement to update all Dashboard injection paths, including endpoint reload, and prove shared-token/password behavior on macOS before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the native Dashboard window and has the strongest traced history on the Dashboard/Gateway auth surface.
